BREAST BEAST

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We exposed a Pretoria GP who has been preforming boob jobs illegally – scarring women for life while the authorities do nothing.

Unique Selling Point:
CLASSIC CARTE BLANCHE
UNDERCOVER
A BADDIE THAT SHOULD BE EXPOSED ONCE AND FOR ALL
PUBLIC INTEREST
PUTTING THE HPCSA ON THE SPOT

Summary:
Plastic Surgery is not something you can just take up as a hobby. You need to get a specialist qualification from a recognised tertiary institution. But in Pretoria, one particular GP, Dr Charl Marais, believes he is exempt from this.

He has been doing what he calls cosmetic surgery for 21 years… One Carte Blanche story, numerous law suits, over 6 complaints at the HPCSA and a string of women that he had scarred for life.

We go back – this time taking on the HPSCA for their inaction and we make sure the Dr Marais gets his camera time.

Further information:
BACKGROUND
CASE STUDY 1
Rochelle Bodenstein (52) went to see Dr Marais last year for a breast reduction and lift. She paid him R50 000 – today her breasts are two different sizes and shapes.

CASE STUDY 2
Jeannie Beegte (30) had a breast reduction done in March, by April she had lost her right breast. Dr. Marais says mistakes happen.

UNDERCOVER
We go undercover to get his sales pitch.

CONFRONT
In 2009 Dr Marais avoided our cameras – his staff alerted him and he did a runner – he sent a legal letter claiming he was acting within his legal parameters.

This time round, we will have a scheduled appointment with a new patient. Then we’ll walk in with cameras, past the reception staff straight into his rooms.

HPCSA
In the 2009, the HPCSA made big promises that GPs doing boob jobs would be stopped – but almost a decade later and a number of complaints against the same offending doctor it seems it really was a case of all talk and no action.

Press Release:


Botched Boob Jobs
From breast implants and reductions, rhinoplasty to liposuction – in recent years, plastic surgery has become more popular with women around the world. It’s a specialised procedure, requiring qualified surgeons and rigorous medical examinations, before the operation. But could your General Practitioner perform a boob job? Despite several law suits, several HPCSA complaints and a string of scarred women, one Pretoria GP has been doing just that – performing cosmetic surgery on breasts for two decades, without any specialist qualifications. Carte Blanche investigates.
Producer: Nicky Troll
Presenter: Devi Sankaree Govender


Script:


STRUCTURE BREAST BEAST

VO: In an age where people are living their so-called best lives on social media, constantly snapping picture perfect moments – there is growing desire for perceived physical perfection.

More and more people want to be nipped, tucked, sucked and plumped all in the name of social acceptance and admiration.

LINK: It’s all about looking your best, preserving youth and keeping up with beauty trends. South Africans are lining up aesthetic surgical procedures dropping millions of rands every year.

VO: And some General Practitioners want in on the action, preforming aesthetic surgical procedures without the regulated training - often with disastrous results.

SNIJMAN: // I am seeing tremendously sub-standard results, am I seeing poorly executed surgery? 100%. INT1 M22

VO: But this is not a new trend. We did our first expose in 2009 and met General Practitioner Dr Charl Marais, who was preforming plastic surgery without the regulated qualifications.

Maryna Wheller went under his knife in 2007 for a breast augmentation - there were serious complications.

UPSOUND CASE STUDY 2009
Maryna: 'I became suicidal. I actually couldn't look at myself. I felt so ugly.'

VO: Fast forward 9 years and he’s still operating on women, masquerading as a so-called cosmetic surgeon.

UPSOUND UNDERCOVER 2018:
DOC: Ek is ‘n cosmetic surgeon. //
PRODUCER 2: Wat is die verskil?
DOC: Ek maak goed mooi – die ander ouens maak gebreekte goed reg [can see face] CLIP3 M9 CLIP5 07:40

SNIJMAN: The term cosmetic surgeon on its own is a misnomer – there is no such thing as a pure cosmetic surgeon. // INT1 M8

VO: Dr Chris Snijman is president of APRASSA – the Association of Plastic, Reconstructive and Aesthetic Surgery of South Africa.

DEVI: Can GPS do Plastic Surgery?
SNIJMAN: I’m sure they can – are they allowed to – the answer is NO.
DEVI: Why not?
SNIJMAN: The initial ruling of the governing body HPCSA which basically states that as a qualified doctor// if you are in the Hinterland and someone comes in with a diagnosis of appendicitis and there is no other surgeon around [and you’ve certain a number that would deem you to be competent] you can go ahead and do an appendectomy. INT1 M13
DEVI: But where is the emergency in a boob job?
SNIJMAN: There is no emergency breast work. //INT1 M15

VO: HPCSA Acting Registrar, Advocate Phelelani Khumalo, explains that medical practitioners must be adequately trained, educated and sufficiently experienced in the procedures they do.

ADV KHUMALO: //in 2013 the board realized they had not sufficiently defined what it would mean to be adequately educated and trained and they then published their interpretation of Rule 21 – which then meant you have to undergo a formal training that is provided by an approved institution by a board approved programme. INT1 M4

VO: But these regulations don’t seem to concern Dr Marais.

DOC: Ek doen dit al vir 21 jaar. Ek doen alles – facelifts, oe, nek, ore, boobs lift, boobies groter maak, reduksie, lipsuction, tummy tucks. CLIP1 M10
PRODUCER: hoeveel van die’s het dokter al gedoen?
DOC: Oh! Duisende CLIP3 M12 // Ons is nie in die gewoonte om kak aan te jaag nie. CLIP1 M11

VO: Rochelle Bodenstein was one of Dr Marais’ recent patients. Having always had big breasts, after three children she wanted a breast lift - but with no implants, because she had ample breasts.

ROCHELLE: // I just wanted them nice and firm again, not smaller. INT1 M3

VO: But that’s not what happened. Dr. Marais did a breast reduction – for which Rochelle signed a consent form. But she says she wasn’t expecting it to be that drastic.

ROCHELLE: I freaked out – I totally freaked out. I was crying and um very emotional. //I said to him this is not what I asked and he said I thought it was best // INT1 M18

VO: Rochelle was left with two different sized breasts, and severe scarring. Dr. Marais was not apologetic at all.

ROCHELLE: // he said were you perfect before… I swear… // I was prepared for the marks but I never expected to have one bigger than the other. INT1 M36
DEVI: How has this impacted on your life?
ROCHELLE: //you can’t wear underwear – even in front of my boyfriend – you don’t want to show him because you’re embarrassed. // I wanted to look better and I look worse. INT1 M30

VO: Interested to see what exactly a consult with Dr Marais entails, we sent in an operative to Centurion Cosmetic Clinic based at Dr Marais’ very own day hospital. The patient wanted change the shape of her breasts, not so much the size.

Dr Marais did two measurements and a fifteen-minute consult to decide on 475 CC implants. We asked Dr Snijman for a comparative consult - it took 30 minutes and 8 measurements. He decided on 275 CC implants.

SNIJMAN: //this massive size discrepancy is disconcordant with the patients request. INT2 M23

VO: If Dr Marais had his way, the patient would have ended up with much bigger breasts despite explicitly saying she didn’t want to go bigger.

While Dr Snijman would insist on seeing the patient a second time before scheduling surgery, Dr. Marais was ready to pick up a scapel.

PRODUCER: …Hoe lank is die waiting period – hoe vol is jy?
DOC: More.
PRODUCER: More. Ok.
DOC: Ek’s vol maar – wie se plek het ek gese is dit?
PRODUCER: Dis joune, // CLIP1 M8
DOC: Ek maak soos ek wil… CLIP1 M9

VO: At just R30700 for implants – it’s around half the ballpark figure most qualified plastic surgeons charge.

Dr Marais’ practice is so busy that he even does breast augmentations having communicated via email with patients and only consulting with them for the first time on the day of surgery.

ANNAMARIE: I went in and that was the first time I met doctor in the operating room INT2 M4

VO: Anna-marie Roos went in for a breast enlargement 18 months ago – she emailed through two measurements and some photos.

Dr Marais then chose 550 CC high profile silicone implants for Anna-marie’s small frame. When she saw the implants, she worried it would be too big.

ANNEMARIE: // he said, you know what it’s not going to be, we’re not going to make you look cheap, we’re just going to make you look sexy – [he actually pulled my boobie like that and said we have to fill this.] INT2 M4

VO: While the procedure went well – Anna-marie’s nightmare was yet to begin.

LINK: It’s often when it comes to complications resulting from procedures that a plastic surgeon’s true skill becomes clear …. falls short….

VO: Anna-marie, had developed capsular contraction as a result of scar tissue in both her breasts – which is a known possible complication of breast augmentation. While she was relieved that Dr. Marais agreed to fix it. Little did she know that she would have to through 5 more surgeries.

Eventually Dr. Marais decided to remove the one implant completely, until the wound had healed – this, took months.
ANNA-MARIE: [cries] You know what you don’t feel like a woman first of all, I had to walk around with pads just to even it out, you cant wear what you want to wear. INT2 M40
VO: In the end, Anna-marie decided to consult a registered plastic surgeon.
APRASSA members are familiar with Dr. Marais’ work, having seen some of his patients.
SNIJMAN: // When it comes down to breast surgery the planning and selection seems to be below par – not to mention the surgical execution. INT1 M37 end

VO: But according to Dr. Marias, specialists have an agenda to keep General Practitioners out of the cosmetic surgery industry because they offer more competitive rates.

LINK: The Health Professions Council of South Africa is tasked with regulating medical practitioners and protecting the public. In 2008 a resolution was passed ruling that only specialists may perform cosmetic procedures.

DEVI: Dr Charl Marais – what is he registered as with the HPCSA?
ADV KHUMALO: in terms of our register – he is registered as a medical practitioner //
DEVI: Should he be preforming plastic surgery?
ADV KHUMALO: Unless he can prove that he has been adequately trained and educated as the board has prescribed – he cannot do it. // INT1 M6

LINK: We’re here at the Centurion Day Clinic – it’s time to say hello, YET again, to Dr Charl Marais….

VO: We went in without requesting an interview, because back in 2009 Dr. Marais avoided us. We had sent in operatives posing as patients.

DEVI: hello, Dr. Marais, We have serious allegations against you. You’ve got more at the HPCSA as you know – I mean why are you still practicing and cutting still people up – why are you still doing boob jobs – you know you are not supposed to do that.
MARAIS: Please leave my room
DEVI: What you have nothing to say?
MARIAS: NO CONFRONT M2
DEVI: –I’ve got other examples of complete botched jobs that have happened, this can’t go on anymore like this.
MARIAS: Really?//
//
MARAIS: [touches devi] Please I ask you….
DEVI: Don’t touch me…
MARAIS: Ok then just go…
DEVI: But are you not going to give us an answer?
MARIAS: No! Kom… [signals cameraman] CONFRONT 5

VO: Subsequently, Dr. Marais responded via email:

He denied any wrong doing in both Rochelle and Anna-marie’s cases, insisted the procedures were done inline with what was discussed and said they never complained to him about the results.

Dr. Marais also stated he gained academic knowledge in cosmetic surgery by extensive reading, studying, attending courses, workshops and congresses. He also worked with a registered plastic surgeon.

But he’s still not registered as a plastic surgeon, nor is he a member of APRASSA.

SNIJMAN: the law as it applies to this country – 4 years recognized institution and pre-requisite examination, our fellowship examination and peer review – so the academy of facial plastic surgery, the clinic of aesthetic breast surgery does not count, youtube does not count. INT1 M32

VO: Dr Marais insists that it’s always been the position that a GPs scope is not limited and that they can preform these procedures if they possess the necessary experience, knowledge and skill.

He also noted that he has preformed 13350 cosmetic procedures and that he had thousands of silent satisfied patients – he added that his success rate is very high, and his complication rate is within acceptable limits.

SNIJMAN: // through our association we have had a number of complaints dating back to 2003. // So, formally bringing it to the registrar’s attention has brought us nowhere in 15 years. INT1 M17

VO: The HPCSA has had 29 complaints, in 10 of the cases Dr Marais was found not guilty – four cases are currently pending, in three, the outcome is unknown, two were closed by the investigator, and 10 were withdrawn.

FIX VOICE – 29 not 18
VO: Asso – if you have 18 complaints – you should be asking what is wrong with me….
ADV KHUMALO: that is their opinion…. Respect that….
DEVI: it’s about upholding standards, // After watching the programme on Sunday you’re going to come to the same conclusion as we have INT1 M24
ADV KHUMALO: That the system is not effective – I take your point ma’am// INT1 M24

VO: But for women like Anna-marie that have been personally affected by Dr Marais - the point – is simple.

ANNEMARIE: If you’re not qualified to do it then you don’t do it – I cant go and fly an airplane – really I can’t. INT2 M35


 
PROMOS

PROMO 1
VO: We exposed a Pretoria GP who has been preforming boob jobs illegally – scarring women for life, while the authorities do nothing.

DOC: Ek doen dit al vir 21 jaar.

PROMO 2
VO: A Pretoria GP has performed plastic surgery without any specialist qualifications for two decades – with devastating consequences.

ROCHELLE: // I was prepared for the marks but I never expected to have one bigger than the other.

PROMO 3
VO: Without specialist qualifications from any registered institution, one Pretoria GP claims to be a cosmetic surgeon.

SNIJMAN: the clinic of aesthetic breast surgery does not count, youtube does not count. INT1 M32

VO: Carte Blanche investigates.


PROMO 4
VO: A Pretoria GP has performed plastic surgery without any specialist qualifications for two decades claiming to be a cosmetic surgeon.

DOC: Ek doen alles – facelifts, oe, nek, ore, boobs lift, boobies groter maak, reduksie, lipsuction, tummy tucks. CLIP1 M10

VO: But the consequences have been devastating in some cases.

ROCHELLE: // I was prepared for the marks but I never expected to have one bigger than the other.

VO: Yet the authorities appear to do nothing.

metadata.Summary: Plastic Surgery is not something you can just take up as a hobby. You need to get a specialist qualification from a recognised tertiary institution. But in Pretoria, one particular GP, Dr Charl Marais, believes he is exempt from this. He has been doing what he calls cosmetic surgery for 21 years… One Carte Blanche story, numerous law suits, over 6 complaints at the HPCSA and a string of women that he had scarred for life. We go back – this time taking on the HPSCA for their inaction and we make sure the Dr Marais gets his camera time.
metadata.Further information: BACKGROUND CASE STUDY 1 Rochelle Bodenstein (52) went to see Dr Marais last year for a breast reduction and lift. She paid him R50 000 – today her breasts are two different sizes and shapes. CASE STUDY 2 Jeannie Beegte (30) had a breast reduction done in March, by April she had lost her right breast. Dr. Marais says mistakes happen. UNDERCOVER We go undercover to get his sales pitch. CONFRONT In 2009 Dr Marais avoided our cameras – his staff alerted him and he did a runner – he sent a legal letter claiming he was acting within his legal parameters. This time round, we will have a scheduled appointment with a new patient. Then we’ll walk in with cameras, past the reception staff straight into his rooms. HPCSA In the 2009, the HPCSA made big promises that GPs doing boob jobs would be stopped – but almost a decade later and a number of complaints against the same offending doctor it seems it really was a case of all talk and no action.
